findings.title: Start storage emulators only for the suites that use them
findings.problem: Each CI run fans out about 200 E2E shards. Every shard spends about 40s starting LocalStack, Azurite, fake-gcs, a Vercel Blob emulator and Redis. About 95% of shards never touch them.
findings.fix: Add storage and redis inputs to the shared start-services action. E2E starts the emulators only for the storage suites.
findings.measured: Over 7.3 days and 690 runs, a sample of 214 runs and 52,161 jobs showed service startup averaging 75s per E2E job.

findings.title: Skip empty "new and changed tests" shards
findings.problem: Every run starts 20 "new and changed tests" shards on 16-core runners. Groups fill from 1 to n, so a PR that touches one test file gets 16 shards that install deps and then print "No added/changed tests detected".
findings.fix: The changes job counts changed test files per mode and emits only min(n, 5) groups. An empty matrix skips the job.
findings.measured: Across 66 runs from Oct 4 to 10, 703 of 820 shard jobs finished in under a minute.

findings.title: Skip secret-dependent matrix legs on fork PRs
findings.problem: Fork PRs don't get secrets, yet 15 cloud and Databricks matrix legs still build and load images, then skip every test.
findings.fix: The set-matrix steps filter out those legs when the PR comes from a fork. Maintainers keep /test-with-secrets.
findings.measured: Oct 4 to 11: 356 of 579 CI runs came from forks. 122 sampled fork runs averaged 9.9 no-op jobs each.

findings.title: Run only the templates a PR changes
findings.problem: Templates is a 25-leg matrix (5 templates x 5 package managers), and every PR runs all of it. Most runs are Dependabot PRs that touch a single template.
findings.fix: A small scope job diffs the commit under test and narrows the matrix to the changed templates. Any other change runs all 25.
findings.measured: Oct 4 to 11: 65 single-template Dependabot runs spent 8,466 rounded min on templates they couldn't affect.
findings.validated: Tested on a fork: changing one template ran 5 legs, a root change ran 25, and a rename ran 10.

findings.title: Warm the mordant cache on main
findings.problem: The mordant-bin cache was only ever saved from PR runs, so every new PR branch rebuilt it from scratch.
findings.fix: Add a path-filtered push trigger on main that only builds and saves the cache. PRs then restore it from the default branch.
findings.measured: In a sample of 62 runs, all 23 misses were a branch's first run, and each miss cost +1.34 rounded min.
findings.validated: Tested on a fork: the push run saved the main cache, and the next PR run hit it.

findings.title: Run the full test tier nightly, as the header says
findings.problem: The workflow header says the full tier is nightly, but 41 full-tier legs also run on every merge to main. Most finish in under a minute.
findings.fix: Gate the 3 full-tier jobs on schedule and workflow_dispatch, the same condition a sibling job already uses.
findings.measured: Oct 10 to 11: the full tier was 79% of push jobs (1,845 of 2,330).
findings.note: Only collaborators can open PRs on this repo, so we filed an issue linking the ready branch.

findings.title: Skip full CI on stacked-PR layers
findings.problem: Stacked-PR layers were 18% of branches but 57% of PR CI runs, and 74% of those runs were cancelled after restacks.
findings.fix: Fall back to uv's own test:skip mode on stack layers unless a label opts in.
findings.measured: Oct 4 to 10: all 1,277 PR CI runs, 58% of them cancelled.
findings.note: Ready on a branch. uv’s contribution policy asks for PRs written and opened by a human, so Austen will open this one himself.

findings.title: Hourly main CI is almost always red
findings.problem: Hourly main CI failed 182 of 183 runs in a week. The biggest single cause is the full-tree dead-code gate (knip), which failed 97 times in about 8 on/off streaks: it doesn’t run on PRs, so unused code lands and gets patched by hand on main. The rest is about 30 unrelated test regressions and flakes.
findings.fix: Run the full-tree knip check on PRs so dead code is caught before merge. That’s a maintainer cost and policy call, not a drive-by PR.
findings.measured: Oct 4 to 12: 183 scheduled runs, 182 failed, 187,765 rounded runner-min.
findings.note: Diagnosed, not shipped. openclaw’s CONTRIBUTING auto-closes PRs that only fix failures already red on main, and their own revert of an earlier “Actions-run savings” PR showed the skipped runs were free.

findings.title: Cancel superseded benchmark runs
findings.problem: The benchmark workflow has no concurrency group, and 30% of PR runs were superseded but still ran all 4 shards.
findings.fix: Add a per-PR concurrency group with cancel-in-progress. Pushes to main stay keyed on run_id, so CodSpeed baselines never cancel.
findings.measured: Oct 8 to 12: 14 of 46 PR benchmark runs were superseded, wasting 274 rounded job-min.

findings.title: Run SDK compatibility tests on the production bundle only in PRs
findings.problem: A non-required SDK compatibility suite runs every host and sample app twice on every PR, once with the production bundle and once with the development bundle. The dev bundle almost never fails on its own.
findings.fix: PRs run the production legs only. Pushes to master still run both bundles.
findings.measured: In 107 sampled PR runs, the dev-bundle legs cost about 35 rounded min per run. The dev bundle failed while prod passed in 1 of 593 pairs.

findings.title: Run shared distribution tests in a single CI job
findings.problem: A 14-leg matrix runs one tiny test suite per shared distribution on every PR. Each leg takes about 20s, mostly checkout and uv install, and asks for 14 of the 20 concurrent jobs Apache allows per workflow.
findings.fix: One job loops over the distributions and fails if any of them fail.
findings.measured: Oct 5 to 11, sampled every 8th of 1,971 runs: these legs were 20.6% of all jobs, and 98.7% finished in under a minute.
findings.validated: All 14 distributions (671 tests) pass locally in 66s, and a forced failure exits 1.

findings.title: Cap blind auto-reruns at two
findings.problem: A temporary workflow reruns the failed jobs of every failed PR CI run up to 3 times. Most runs that reach attempt 4 still fail on the same jobs, so the reruns only delay a red signal.
findings.fix: Allow two blind reruns instead of three. The third rerun rescued only 8 of 63 runs (13%), and dropping it turns deterministic failures red about 9 minutes sooner.
findings.measured: Oct 4 to 11: 58 of 599 CI runs reached attempt 4 and 46 still failed. In 8 of 9 sampled runs, the same jobs failed on every attempt.
findings.note: About 8 PRs a week will need a manual rerun.

findings.title: Queue push-to-main runs instead of stacking them
findings.problem: The "nightly" workflow also runs the full 13-library suite on every merge to main. Each run takes about 3 hours, so 89 of 98 push runs in a week overlapped one another.
findings.fix: A concurrency group queues push-to-main runs without cancelling, so main is still tested at its newest commit. Scheduled and manual runs are keyed by run ID and never queue.
findings.measured: 98 push runs/week, p50 183 min, ~9.2k job-min per run (sampled n=12). Replaying the queue gives ~32 runs/week.

findings.title: Skip re-running checks for PR title and body edits on a passing commit
findings.problem: Editing a PR's title or body fires pull_request `edited`, which re-ran CI, regression and Windows render on a commit that had already passed.
findings.fix: A small composite action skips the check jobs only when the previous run on the same head SHA succeeded and the base branch didn't change. Failed or unfinished predecessors still re-run everything, so a body edit can't turn a failed required check green.
findings.measured: Last 7 days: 1,205 edit reruns followed a passing run on the same SHA and burned ~129k job-min. 20 sampled reruns had no base change.

findings.title: Stop auto-updating Dependabot and Renovate PRs behind main
findings.problem: A Mergify rule merged main into every open Dependabot/Renovate PR whenever main moved, re-running full CI each time. It dates from when branches had to be up to date; the repo now uses a merge queue.
findings.fix: Remove the Mergify update rule and Renovate's rebase-when-behind setting. The merge queue still tests each PR against current main.
findings.measured: Oct 5 to 11: Mergify pushed 314 merge commits to 27 bot branches, triggering 4,309 runs (85% of runs on those branches). One PR was updated 32 times.

findings.title: Skip Slow on draft pull requests
findings.problem: The Slow suite ran on every push to every PR, including drafts that nobody was ready to review.
findings.fix: Skip Slow jobs on draft PRs and run them on opened and ready_for_review. Main, merge queue and required-check names are unchanged, and maintainers can still dispatch it manually.
findings.measured: 7 days: 276 of 591 Slow PR runs (47%) fired on drafts. Net of ready_for_review reruns, ~85-95k min/week is avoidable.

findings.title: Test fewer Redis versions on pull requests
findings.problem: Every PR push tested against 9 Redis server versions, 234 test jobs per run.
findings.fix: PRs test 3 versions: the preview, current stable and oldest supported. Pushes to master and release branches, plus nightly, still run all 9.
findings.measured: Oct 5 to 12, 547 runs: the 6 dropped versions were 39.6% of PR CI minutes (sampled 82 runs, all attempts).

findings.title: Restore Rust caches from main instead of saving per-PR
findings.problem: Every PR job saved its own Rust cache, overflowing the 10 GB repo limit and evicting main's entries. The whole cache turned over in about 7 minutes, so 90% of sampled jobs missed.
findings.fix: Add `save-if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'` to the 27 unguarded rust-cache steps, matching 11 steps the repo already guarded.
findings.measured: 680 of 756 sampled ci-cua-sdk jobs missed cache. Cache hits ran 30-70% faster (e.g. macOS smoke 28.5 vs 63.4 min). Savings depend on the post-fix hit rate: ~65-104k min/week.

findings.title: Cancel superseded pull request runs
findings.problem: System Tests had no concurrency group, so when a PR got a new push the old run kept going to completion.
findings.fix: PR-only cancel-in-progress. Push, merge queue and schedule runs are keyed by run ID, the same pattern dd-trace-java uses.
findings.measured: 774 PR runs/week, 0 cancelled, 190 superseded runs finished anyway at ~267 job-min each (sampled n=30).

findings.title: Add configurable timeouts for Linux, Static SDK, Wasm and Android builds
findings.problem: Nightly-toolchain jobs in this shared reusable workflow can hang until GitHub kills them at 6 hours, and every package that calls it inherits the hang.
findings.fix: Add timeout inputs with a 90-minute default.
findings.measured: Sep 27 to Oct 10: swift-network-evolution alone lost ~48k min/week to hung jobs in this workflow.

findings.title: Add a job timeout to the shared test matrix workflow
findings.problem: Nightly-toolchain test jobs from this shared matrix hang until the 6-hour limit in downstream repos like swift-nio-quic and swift-http-server.
findings.fix: Add a timeout_minutes input, default 120.
findings.measured: Sep 27 to Oct 10: ~25k min/week hung in swift-nio-quic and ~9k in swift-http-server.

findings.title: Add timeout to macOS Psalm scan job
findings.problem: The macOS scan build hangs until the 6-hour limit.
findings.fix: A 15-minute job timeout.
findings.measured: Sep 27 to Oct 10: ~19k min/week in hung jobs.

findings.title: Add a job timeout to the ROS2 test workflows
findings.problem: webots_ros2_tiago tests hang inside industrial_ci until the 6-hour limit.
findings.fix: A 60-minute job timeout on both test workflows.
findings.measured: Sep 27 to Oct 10: ~16.6k min/week in hung jobs.

findings.title: Add a 20-minute timeout to the CI build jobs
findings.problem: A streaming test never returns after a 503, so builds ran to the 6-hour limit.
findings.fix: A 20-minute job timeout.
findings.measured: Sep 27 to Oct 10: ~11.5k min/week in hung jobs.

findings.title: Add a 45-minute timeout to split-units jobs
findings.problem: Bigtable, Pub/Sub and Spanner unit test shards occasionally hang until the 6-hour limit.
findings.fix: A 45-minute timeout on split-units.
findings.measured: Sep 27 to Oct 10: ~6.1k min/week in hung jobs.

findings.title: Time out the quickcheck property tests after 10 minutes
findings.problem: The publish_with_expiration quickcheck property test hangs until the 6-hour limit.
findings.fix: A 10-minute step timeout.
findings.measured: Sep 27 to Oct 10: ~6k min/week in hung jobs.

findings.title: Add a 90-minute timeout to the selenium jobs
findings.problem: Stalled selenium jobs ran to the 6-hour limit.
findings.fix: A 90-minute job timeout.
findings.measured: Sep 27 to Oct 10: ~5.9k min/week in hung jobs.

findings.title: Start image-consuming test jobs after image builds
findings.problem: Test jobs start alongside the image builds and poll for about 3 minutes per leg until the images exist.
findings.fix: `needs: build` on the 12 image-consuming test jobs across 7 workflows, for about +1 min wall clock per workflow.
findings.measured: n=12 runs per workflow over exact 7-day run counts: ~117k of ~710k job-min/week in these workflows.
findings.note: Non-member PRs need a maintainer-labeled issue, and the overlap was a deliberate latency trade-off, so we filed an issue with the ready branch.

findings.title: Daily HGraph concurrent-add test hangs until the 6-hour limit
findings.problem: A deadlock in the daily HGraph Concurrent Add test means the nightly hasn't passed in 400 runs.
findings.fix: Fix the deadlock, and bound the job with a timeout once maintainers give a runtime estimate.
findings.measured: Sep 27 to Oct 10: ~7.7k min/week in hung jobs.
findings.note: Filed as an issue because the right timeout needs a maintainer estimate.

findings.title: Hosted wait-for-* jobs poll while GPU stages run
findings.problem: GitHub-hosted wait-for-* jobs poll for earlier test stages so PR stages run A then B then C. Two hit the 6-hour limit in a week.
findings.fix: Replace polling with needs:. But labels like parallel-stages switch the order at runtime, which static needs: can't express, so it needs a maintainer design call.
findings.measured: Oct 4 to 11, sampled 1,741 runs: waiters ~205k min/week (90% CI 164-255k), ~29% of hosted minutes.

findings.title: Run the full suite only at the ends of a PR stack
findings.problem: 210 of 276 recent PRs are GitHub-native stacks. Every layer runs the full test suite, and a branches filter can't help because each layer evaluates as targeting main.
findings.fix: Run the 9 test jobs on the lowest unmerged and top layers only, with the required check still reporting. This reverses a deliberate maintainer change, so it's their call.
findings.measured: test.yaml 1,302 runs/week, ~411k job-min. Mid-stack runs: 477/week at ~320 min (sampled n=148).

findings.title: Skip scheduled stable-branch runs when HEAD hasn't changed
findings.problem: Every ~6 hours a schedule dispatches full e2e suites on each stable branch, even when the branch HEAD is unchanged.
findings.fix: A stateless check skips a branch already dispatched at the same HEAD in the last 20 hours. New commits are still tested within ~6 hours.
findings.measured: Oct 5 to 12: 84 stable-branch firings covered only 27 distinct HEADs; 57 re-tested the previous HEAD.
findings.note: A community PR (cilium/cilium#49001) already proposes this, and Cilium doesn't accept AI-written PR text, so we're offering the cache-free variant to that author rather than opening a competing PR.
